extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communications teams, marketers, and anyone writing and distributing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for creating newsworthy press releases and distributing them to the right media using good editorial practices, multimedia, personalization, and AI-assisted workflows. Includes best practices, anti-patterns, examples, and pitching/distribution steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use visual storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release rich in captivating images, infographics, and videos can break through the noise and leave a lasting impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make visuals catchy but aligned with brand messaging. Consider placing a photo at the top to illustrate how something works (example: Klarna). Visuals should complement and immediately grab reader attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilize interactive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore interactive content formats such as interactive graphics or multimedia experiences to make news more engaging for your audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of static screenshots, embed social media posts or add videos (e.g., via Press Release Creator blocks). Interactive features increase retention and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize for mobile devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure press releases look good on mobile: be responsive and fast-loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both creation and distribution UX. Most readers check news via smartphones, so mobile responsiveness and speed are press release UX best practices to follow before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include visualizations of your data
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform complex data and statistics into visually captivating charts and graphs to make releases more trustworthy and engaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visualized data informs and impresses while avoiding burying the message in raw numbers. Add your logo to infographics to preserve source attribution. If the infographic covers a hot topic it may be shared widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalize outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor your message and outreach efforts to specific journalists or media outlets rather than sending generic pitches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate genuine understanding of journalists' interests and beats. Personalization is a key trend—customize content and pitching to increase response and coverage rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer exclusive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Add exclusive content or insights to secure coverage and build relationships with editors and journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using exclusive content, consider pitching directly to journalists instead of using newswires to increase chances of pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver social proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Include testimonials, user reviews, or quotes from industry experts to back up claims in your press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social proof increases credibility; incorporate UGC or expert endorsements into the release structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight human interest stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Include personal anecdotes or the story of an individual (employee, beneficiary, etc.) to engage readers emotionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Storytelling and human faces help cut through information overload. Reserve space in your template for human-focused narrative elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address a current problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Connect your announcement to a real, current problem that matters to readers, using specific numbers where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate news to broader issues (example: Starbucks and resource positivity). Specific, measurable claims strengthen credibility; a concise headline helps too.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer a multimedia press kit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comprehensive multimedia assets—images, videos, fact sheets, quotations—to equip journalists with resources for coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A multimedia press kit can be attached to the release or hosted in an Online Newsroom. These assets also serve as exclusive content for journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilize influencer partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborate with social media influencers, industry personas, or brand ambassadors to extend the reach of your press release across their platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage influencer shoutouts and partnerships to amplify distribution and audience reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor hot topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Stay informed about trending topics across the web and incorporate relevant trends into your release to boost relevance and visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social media monitoring tools and guides to identify topical hooks that can be added as 'cherry on top' to your story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize statements by leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes or statements from C-level executives to provide deeper insights, informed perspectives, or authoritative commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership quotes help provide 'behind the scenes' insight and lend authority; they should add analysis or context rather than generic PR platitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight diversity and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Underscore a genuine dedication to diversity and inclusion by showcasing a variety of voices and representations in content and visuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid tokenism — make D&I part of strategy and authentic practice. Superficial inclusion risks reputational harm if exposed as PR only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and measure results
rubrics_metrics.description: Track metrics like media exposure, domain rank, backlinks, social interactions, and sentiment analysis to gauge impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide stakeholders with actionable reporting (PR Clippings, alternative metrics to advertising value equivalency or UVPM). Use tools to aggregate and present performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize for SEO and voice search (advanced tip)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include natural language phrases and answer common questions to improve discoverability in voice search (Siri, Alexa) and SEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write content that mirrors conversational queries and provides clear answers to likely user questions, especially if publishing to an Online Newsroom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hidden Lead (don't)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not conceal the most crucial information deep within the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the inverted pyramid method: lead with the most important information so journalists discover the vital details right away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Too salesy (don't)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid making a press release read like a promotional sales pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists may disregard overly promotional content as biased or lacking credibility. Keep tone informative and news-focused rather than sales-oriented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect personalized pitches (don't)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not distribute generic pitches to journalists without tailoring them to beats or interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generic pitching leads to low response rates; use personalization tools and manual tailoring to improve outreach effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forget multimedia assets (don't)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to include relevant multimedia like images or videos lessens a release's attractiveness and shareability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include ready-to-use assets to make it easier for reporters to cover the story; missing assets reduce pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miss out on AI (don't)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid ignoring AI tools that can speed drafting, suggest subject lines, and help identify contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI can be a useful assistant for drafts, pitches, and contact suggestions—don't forgo its efficiency gains (but apply human editing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI to write initial drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: AI can help create a first draft, overcome writer's block, and ensure key aspects of the story are covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI assistance can draft quotes, reduce overly-salesy language, and save time — use it as a starting point, then edit for accuracy and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI to deliver the message (three key messages)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI can help you stay focused by distilling the story into three key messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write down three key messages and use AI to ensure the release communicates them clearly; this keeps the narrative on track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI to answer crucial questions
rubrics_metrics.description: AI tools can prompt you to answer a series of questions to surface key details for the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide initial information and let AI ask follow-up questions to fill in missing facts and strengthen the release copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI to adjust tone of voice
rubrics_metrics.description: AI can adjust the tone of the press release according to the chosen story angle (e.g., friendly/excited vs empathetic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a consistent tone of voice aligned with brand and story (examples: more friendly/excited for an event; more empathetic for charity communications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft the pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: When pitching, attach or embed the press release and draft a tailored email pitch for selected recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI can generate a preliminary pitch from the release; structure the pitch to present four key messages in bullets for quick journalist scanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a catchy subject line
rubrics_metrics.description: Use compelling subject lines and preview text to increase open rates in journalists' crowded inboxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI can suggest subject line options — customize and test to find the best fit and improve engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find the right media contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Build and expand a targeted list of journalists and outlets filtered by language, topics, and beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use media databases (e.g., Prowly) or AI: type the first ~100 words of your pitch and get AI suggestions for journalists to pitch based on keywords found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow press release structure / inverted pyramid
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard press release structure and the inverted pyramid to ensure clarity and journalistic usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep writing concise and informative (example: Apple product release praised for concise, informative style). Lead with the most important facts, then provide supporting details.
